overall_assessment.realism: The samples are highly realistic, reflecting common credential harvesting phishing tactics such as domain homoglyphs, typosquatting, recent domain registrations, failed SPF/DMARC checks, and plausible email content impersonating trusted entities. The technical details including email headers, SMTP logs, domain registration info, HTTP requests/responses, and WAF logs are detailed and consistent with real-world phishing campaigns. The scenarios cover diverse targets (financial, HR, cloud storage) and include appropriate indicators and detection methods aligned with current cybersecurity practices.
overall_assessment.consistency: The samples maintain strong consistency and adhere well to the expected schema. Each entry includes scenario description, detailed technical data with nested structures, indicators, detection methods, and relevant MITRE ATT&CK techniques. Field naming and data types are uniform across samples. Minor variations in registrar naming (e.g., 'GoDaddy.com, LLC' vs 'GoDaddy') are present but do not significantly impact schema adherence. The use of timestamps, IP addresses, and domain names is coherent and internally consistent within each sample.
suggestions: Standardize registrar naming conventions across all samples for uniformity (e.g., always use full official registrar names).
Include DKIM and DMARC results explicitly in the 'Authentication-Results' header for all samples, even if 'none' or 'fail', to enhance completeness.
Add more variation in user-agent strings in HTTP requests to simulate diverse victim environments.
Incorporate some samples with partial or successful SPF/DKIM to reflect more sophisticated phishing attempts.
Consider adding examples of multi-factor authentication bypass or token theft to expand scenario diversity.
Include explicit mention of the phishing email's MIME boundary or multipart structure if applicable, to increase email realism.
Add more detailed WAF rule triggers or alerts in some samples to illustrate detection nuances.
